children: H&M faces fading earnings momentum and little to justify the stock's current valuation, Pareto Securities analysts Kristian Smolle and Alexander Siljestrom write. Fiscal fourth-quarter guidance was soft, flagging rising freight costs, higher discounts, and a step-up in overhead costs, they say. These headwinds extend into 2027 on top of higher IT investments, while H&M continues to struggle to engage its customers, they add. On the back of the soft guidance and a third quarter underlying gross margin that came in below expectations, Pareto Securities cuts its adjusted EBIT estimates by 1%-3% for 2026-2028. "We expect shares to de-rate further." The bank lowers its target price to 135 Swedish kronor from 140 kronor and retains its sell rating. Shares fall 0.6% to 161.80 kronor. (dominic.chopping@wsj.com)
